messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — running a key-rotation + simulated CMK failure drill tomorrow 09:30 PT. Goal: exercise restore path for snapshots and backup decrypt when primary CMK unavailable. Outline below, need volunteers and owners.

sam: I'm in. Can we scope to prod replicas only? don't want to touch primary DB during business hours.

maria: Yes — we'll do read-only replicas and backup restores in a sandboxed account. Intend to test cross-account grant flow + ephemeral grants. No writes to prod.

alyssa: Suggest we validate audit logging before the drill — I want to ensure KMS Grant/Decrypt events appear in CloudTrail and our ingest pipeline. Otherwise alerts won't trigger.

jordan: +1. I'll add a pre-check step: run `aws kms get-key-rotation-status` and `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt` against the test account.

leo: Who's owning the RBAC changes? We'll need a short-lived role for the rotation agent and an uploader SA for backup restores.

maria: @leo you OK to own RBAC? I'll own the playbook and coord with infra to create an ephemeral grant script.

leo: yep I'll prepare an IAM doc. Plan: create `rotate-drill-role` with sts:AssumeRole, limit to kms:Decrypt, kms:CreateGrant and put a 10m session duration. We'll attach a condition restricting to `aws:SourceArn` of the restore job.

maria: Nice. For audit, add a tag in the grant like `RotationDrill=true` so we can filter events. Also ensure the backup uploader logs include `grantId` in metadata.

encops-bot: NOTE: This drill touches CMK policies. Please post CMK ARNs and confirm HSM-based keys not impacted. Scheduled window: 09:30-10:30 PT.

sam: Quick question — if the simulated failure is "primary CMK disabled", do we also simulate grant expiry? which is higher fidelity?

maria: Let's do both in separate runs: first disable CMK (block decrypt), then restore and run a grant-expiry scenario where we revoke the ephemeral grant mid-restore. Observability team: will you capture correlation IDs?

alyssa: I can capture CloudTrail + our internal audit logs. I'll create a saved query and shared dashboard (link will be posted).

jordan: For restore steps include the following snippet in the runbook:
```
# assume role
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/rotate-drill-role --role-session-name drill
# request grant
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-backup-key --grantee-principal arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/rotate-drill-role/drill --operations Decrypt
# run restore
restore-tool --backup s3://redwood-backups/drill/2026-03-xx --decrypt-with-grant
```

leo: I'll prepare the IAM patch and post it in #eng-security as a PR link. Also will include short rollback steps if something flaps.

maria: Thanks. Volunteers: @sam restore lead, @alyssa observability, @leo rbac, @jordan runbook + scripts. If anyone else wants to jump in ping me. Will post the final playbook and pre-check checklist later today.

sam: Acked. I'll carve out time.

alyssa: One more ask — ensure we capture any unexpected `AccessDenied` error codes with full context (grantId, keyId, principal). We should map them to our incident taxonomy.

maria: Will do. After the drill, we'll run a 30m blameless retro in #eng-postmortems. If anyone has concerns about the scope speak up now.

jordan: FYI I ran a quick smoke in staging — creating a grant with `Constraints: EncryptionContext:stringEquals:{ \"purpose\":\"drill\"}` worked fine. I'll add that to the template.

encops-bot: REMINDER: create backup of CMK policy before changes. Auto-check will fail if policy diff > 5 lines.

leo: PR posted: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/rotate-drill-iam.patch

maria: Thanks all. See you tomorrow 09:30 PT. :thumbsup:
